article.title: What we talk about when we talk about US strategic ‘credibility’ – from Vietnam to Iran
article.summary:
Either way, most observers insist that for the United States, “credibility is on the line in Iran.” But that has long been a central concern of U.S. foreign policy.
Historical examples are useful here, in particular the Vietnam War, during which American credibility was at stake in unprecedented ways.
Yet policymakers repeatedly insisted that Vietnam was the place where American credibility had to be demonstrated and established.
Counterintuitively, while the Vietnam War was fought in the eyes of many policymakers to defend U.S. credibility, its conclusion shattered conventional notions of credibility.
But the problem, as it was in the Vietnam War, is that credibly engaging in war and violence is not a substitute for strategy.
